intelligence.human_view: A list of names with percentages is a directory, not a connection. The moment the row carries its four buttons — message, mail, audio, video — it stops being a list and becomes a door: one tap and you are talking to the person. He saw that the rows were off-centered and the controls were missing, and then he answered his own question the way only the person who will use it can: people do not discover what is hidden. They discover what is shown. "Oh wow, I can just message them. So simple." — that is the whole product in one sentence. The button does not add a feature; it reveals one that was already there. Every capability we hide behind a menu or a guess is a capability nobody uses, and a capability nobody uses might as well not exist.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine a classroom where you can talk to anyone — but there's no button to do it, so nobody knows they can. Shawn says: put the buttons right there in the row, where you can see them — message, mail, audio, video. Then you look at the row and think, "Oh wow, I can just message them. So simple!" If you can't see it, you can't use it. The button is what turns a list of names into a real connection.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, Shawn looked at the rows of people and said the buttons should be right there where you can see them, dear — message, mail, audio, video, all in a neat line. Because if people can't see that they can just message someone, they won't know they can, dear. But when the button is right there, they think, "Oh wow, I can just message them. So simple!" That's the whole thing, dear — you have to show people what they can do, or they never do it.
intelligence.naya_view: PEOPLE USE WHAT THEY CAN SEE. A CAPABILITY NOBODY SEES IS A CAPABILITY NOBODY USES. THE VISIBLE BUTTON TURNS A LIST OF NAMES INTO A CONNECTION.
